input.text: Why are you always on the market square?

requestBody.message: Why are you always on the market square?

chunks.text:
data: {"type":"tool","id":"tool-1","name":"ask_pigeon"}

data: {"type":"text","delta":"I will ask the pigeon why the bustling environment of the market square is so central to its presence in the city."}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":"My available sources do not have any data on why I am always at the market square. However, I go there because"}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":" that is where the action and the food crumbs are. Why should we stay away from the liveliest spot in our own city?"}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":" The market square is our living room, and we refuse to be pushed out of it."}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" a shared space where human activity and animal survival directly overlap, creating an inevitable friction over who belongs in the city's busiest areas"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":". While people often design these squares for commerce, leisure, and cleanliness, the pigeon views the resulting concentration of food as a vital resource for its"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" community. Deciding how to manage this space means choosing between strict control of public areas and accepting a shared, multi-species environment. \n\nHow"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" can city planners balance the demand for clean plazas with the reality that human activity naturally draws other urban inhabitants?"}
